chains.title: TFAP2E/AP-2 is predicted to bind the ref allele more strongly at a cryptic intronic site
chains.element: PYDC2-AS1 intron, 42 bp from dELS EH38E2269392

links.claim: TFAP2E/AP-2 is predicted to bind the ref T allele more strongly than the alt G allele (QBiC-SELEX effect -0.765, z -18.37). The AP-2 signal is family-ambiguous: TFAP2A, TFAP2C, and TFAP2E share the same TFAP2E-mapped model and identical effect statistics, so TFAP2E is named only because it has the highest HCT116 expression and an own model among the AP-2 candidates; no ENCODE ChIP-seq peak contains the variant, and TFAP2A ChIP-seq in HCT116 shows no peak, although absence can reflect no experiment.

The variant is intronic in PYDC2-AS1 and does not overlap a cCRE; the nearest element is a dELS 42 bp away, and its reported z-scores are maxima over ENCODE biosamples, so a functional AP-2 site here would be cryptic and non-registry.
PYDC2 is the nearest protein-coding gene at 19.5 kb, but no GTEx v8 eQTL links this variant to PYDC2 expression, including in Colon Transverse, leaving the target gene uncertain.

HCT116 is the expression context, and TFAP2E is expressed there at 8.5 TPM, higher than the other AP-2 candidates, but there is no HCT116 ChIP evidence showing AP-2 occupancy at this site and the family signal is not uniquely attributable to TFAP2E.

Any colorectal cancer effect would require altered AP-2 occupancy to change PYDC2 or nearby gene expression; current genetic and literature evidence do not establish this chain, and the expression direction is unknown because AP-2 factors can activate or repress.

predictions: AP-2 family ChIP or an allele-specific reporter assay in HCT116 would show stronger binding or activity for the ref T allele than for the alt G allele.
TFAP2E knockdown would reduce the allele-specific AP-2 effect if TFAP2E is the relevant family member.
PYDC2 or nearby gene expression would change with the allele if this element is functional.
falsified_if: No AP-2 family occupancy is detected at this base in HCT116.
TFAP2E is not the relevant AP-2 factor, or the allele effect is absent or reversed.
The variant does not affect PYDC2 or nearby gene expression.

chains.title: EBF4 is predicted to bind the ref allele more strongly at a cryptic intronic site
chains.element: PYDC2-AS1 intron, 42 bp from dELS EH38E2269392

links.claim: EBF4 is predicted to bind the ref T allele more strongly than the alt G allele (QBiC-SELEX effect -1.954, z -60.28). EBF4 was chosen because it has the largest QBiC-SELEX allele effect among the candidates, but occupancy is unknown: no ENCODE ChIP-seq peak contains this variant and EBF4 was never assayed by ENCODE; EBF4 is also expressed at only 1.22 TPM in HCT116.

The variant is intronic in PYDC2-AS1 and does not overlap a registered cCRE; the nearest element is a dELS 42 bp away, and its reported chromatin z-scores are maxima over ENCODE biosamples rather than HCT116-specific evidence.
PYDC2 is the nearest protein-coding gene at 19.5 kb, but no GTEx v8 eQTL links this variant to PYDC2 expression, including in Colon Transverse, so the target-gene assignment is speculative.

HCT116 is the supplied expression context, and EBF4 is expressed there at a low level (1.22 TPM, rank 988/1626); this is compatible with but does not demonstrate a functional EBF4 role in this cell type, and no HCT116 occupancy evidence exists.

A colorectal cancer effect would require allele-specific EBF4 occupancy to change PYDC2 or nearby gene expression; current GWAS, Open Targets, eQTL, and literature evidence do not establish this chain, and the direction of any expression effect is unknown because EBF4 could activate or repress.

EBF4 knockdown would reduce the allele-specific effect if EBF4 is the responsible factor.

The allele-specific binding effect is absent or reversed in an occupancy assay.
No change in PYDC2 or nearby gene expression is linked to the variant.

No ENCODE ChIP-seq peak contains the variant and ETV3 was never assayed by ENCODE, so occupancy is unknown.
The variant is intronic in PYDC2-AS1 and does not overlap a cCRE; the nearest element is a dELS 42 bp away, so an ETV3 site here would be cryptic and not supported by current cCRE annotation.
PYDC2 is the nearest protein-coding gene at 19.5 kb, but no GTEx v8 eQTL links this variant to PYDC2 expression, including in Colon Transverse, so the target gene is not established.

HCT116 is the expression context, and ETV3 is expressed there at 16.34 TPM, but there is no HCT116 ChIP evidence showing ETV3 occupancy at this site, and the binding prediction comes from a mapped ETV5 model at a weak site.

A colorectal cancer effect would require allele-specific ETV3 occupancy to alter PYDC2 or nearby gene expression; current GWAS, Open Targets, eQTL, and literature evidence do not establish this, and the direction of any expression change is unknown because ETV3 could activate or repress.

The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th.
